ns2:section.sectionText: Meets w/HIST 385 (CRN 61655) Description: This course takes transnational and comparative approaches to analyses of sexuality and gender. Comparing and connecting U.S. contexts with examples from societies in the Middle East, East Asia, Africa, Europe, and Latin America, it looks at diverse sexuality and gender systems from the classical to modern era and explores how gender and sexuality as modern categories have intersected with one another in their construction of differences and hierarchies.
